title: Bone tissue and the skeleton
note: The adult skeleton has 206 bones: 80 axial (skull, vertebral column, thoracic cage) and 126 appendicular (limbs and girdles). Osteoblasts build bone, osteocytes maintain it, and osteoclasts resorb it. Compact bone is built of osteons; spongy bone is a lattice of trabeculae.

read.title: Bone is living tissue
text: It is easy to picture bone as dead and fixed, but bone is a living tissue that is rebuilt throughout life. Three cell types do the work. Osteoblasts lay down new matrix of collagen and calcium salts. Some become trapped in what they build and mature into osteocytes, which sit in small spaces called lacunae and help maintain the surrounding mineral. Osteoclasts, large cells with many nuclei, dissolve bone where it is not needed.

Compact bone, the dense outer layer of every bone, is organized into osteons. Each osteon is a set of concentric rings of matrix around a central canal that carries blood vessels and nerves. Tiny canaliculi link the lacunae to each other and to the canal, so nutrients and wastes can reach every osteocyte.

Spongy bone, inside the ends of long bones, has no osteons. It is a lattice of thin plates called trabeculae that line up along the directions of stress, giving strength with little weight. The spaces between trabeculae in many bones hold red marrow, where blood cells are made.
A long bone shows both types: a hollow shaft, the diaphysis, walled with compact bone, and two wider ends, the epiphyses, filled with spongy bone.

q.q: How do nutrients reach osteocytes in compact bone?
o: Through canaliculi linked to the central canal
